rv.q: In this pure, funny, beautifully bittersweet Goodman production of Chekhov's last play, the source of humor is well-pinpointed in humans' fundamental inability to change.
It's not only a tautly adapted and directed play, but a masterclass in acting.
You won't be quick to forget this epic night at the theatre.
It is theater of the highest caliber, a classic running spritely on all cylinders with production values that are rich, textured and sublime.
THE CHERRY ORCHARD is a perfect farewell for Robert Falls' long reign as Artistic Director. It's a charmingly hilarious and hopeful tribute to what comes next.
The grand set, the top-flight actors, the whip-smart adaptation and direction that give Chekhov's 1903 play palpable relevance in 2023, it's the recipe for a bittersweet masterpiece.
But, despite its length and leisurely pacing, 'The Cherry Orchard' will undoubtedly stand out as one of his finest contributions to Chicago Theatre.
With all this talent on stage, they could be doing a play about eating pizza, which would be a hit!
Thank you, Robert Falls, for a wonderful, doubly poignant exit.
Falls has chosen his swan song well. This is a play about looking back to see what once was and reflecting on what might never have been.

Fry brings a lovely wistfulness to Renevskaya's sense of connection to the home and orchard, and to the privileged life she is losing. But a more intense sense of loss (and even bitterness) is needed to anchor this play.
Rich and masterful, 'The Cherry Orchard' serves as a triumphant curtain for Robert Falls' Goodman Theatre tenure.
I strongly recommend seeing it before it leaves The Goodman!
Directed by Robert Falls, who up until now has never directed this play, using his own adaptation, he has assembled an all-star cast of Chicago talent to bring this story to life, 'his way'!

cn.t: Robert Falls' adaptation of Chekhov's classic serves as a triumphant farewell to his Goodman Theatre tenure, with critics praising its surprisingly comedic tone and masterful direction that balances humor with profound emotional depth.
